formulations.name: Nondimensionalization
formulations.meaning: Rescales physical variables using characteristic quantities.
formulations.purpose: Reduces scale disparity while preserving a dimensionally transformed governing problem.
formulations.relation: It acts as numerical preconditioning before loss balancing and optimization.
formulations.symbols: \(L_0,T_0,U_s\): characteristic scales; hats denote nondimensional variables.

formulations.name: Normalized multi-term scalarization
formulations.meaning: Scales heterogeneous objective components before combining them.
formulations.purpose: Reduces domination caused by units or magnitude differences.
formulations.relation: It is a normalized extension of the canonical weighted composite loss.

formulations.name: Adaptive loss weighting
formulations.meaning: Updates loss weights during training using loss or gradient information.
formulations.purpose: Attempts to keep competing physical/data objectives from becoming numerically unbalanced.
formulations.relation: It makes scalarization dynamic rather than fixed.

formulations.name: Gradient-norm balancing target
formulations.meaning: Expresses the goal of balancing gradient contributions from competing objective terms.
formulations.purpose: Targets optimization imbalance at the gradient level rather than only matching scalar loss magnitudes.
formulations.relation: It provides a diagnostic/design principle for adaptive weighting methods.

formulations.name: Bounded-mask self-adaptive point weighting
formulations.meaning: Uses trainable nonnegative self-adaptation variables passed through a nondecreasing bounded mask so points with persistent residual error can receive greater emphasis while the inner maximization remains finite for fixed \(\theta\).
formulations.purpose: Captures the soft-attention/self-adaptive PINN mechanism without the unbounded linear-weight maximization of the previous catalogue equation.
formulations.relation: The cited SA-PINN formulation allows increasing mask functions such as polynomial or sigmoidal masks; bounded sigmoidal masks satisfy the displayed condition directly, while polynomial masks require the practical upper cap described by the method to avoid unbounded growth/overflow.
formulations.symbols: \(\lambda_i\): trainable self-adaptation variable; \(g\): nonnegative nondecreasing mask; \(g_{max}<\infty\): mask upper bound/cap.

formulations.name: Gradient-enhanced physics loss
formulations.meaning: Penalizes derivatives of the governing residual in addition to the residual itself.
formulations.purpose: Provides higher-order local information to training.
formulations.relation: It augments rather than replaces the canonical PINN loss.
formulations.symbols: \(\omega_g\): gradient-residual weight; \(\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}r_\theta\): residual gradient with respect to inputs.

formulations.name: Loss-informed importance-sampling density
formulations.meaning: Constructs a normalized sampling density over the actual residual-sampling support, favoring locations with larger current pointwise loss/residual.
formulations.purpose: Allocates collocation effort toward difficult regions while remaining valid when residual inputs include parameters, geometry descriptors, or variables beyond space and time.
formulations.relation: It makes point selection part of the evolving optimization problem without assuming that every catalogue input lives only in \(\Omega\times(0,T]\).
formulations.symbols: \(\rho\): base sampling density; \(\ell_\theta\): nonnegative pointwise loss indicator; \(\alpha\ge0\): concentration parameter; \(\mathcal{X}_r\): residual-sampling support in the full input space.

formulations.name: Residual-based adaptive sampling
formulations.meaning: Samples or resamples collocation points according to the magnitude of the current scalar or vector residual field.
formulations.purpose: Improves local coverage where physical violations remain large.
formulations.relation: It closes a feedback loop between model error indicators and the training distribution; for scalar residuals the Euclidean norm reduces to absolute value.

formulations.name: Neural tangent kernel for scalar and vector PINN outputs
formulations.meaning: Defines the scalar-output NTK and its matrix-valued extension for vector physical states using the output Jacobian with respect to trainable parameters.
formulations.purpose: Analyzes training dynamics, spectral behavior, and imbalance while matching the Atlas distinction between scalar and vector-valued PINN outputs.
formulations.relation: The scalar kernel is recovered as the one-output special case of the matrix-valued kernel; this remains a training-theory diagnostic rather than a new physical residual.
formulations.symbols: \(J_\theta(\boldsymbol{\xi})=\partial\mathbf{u}_\theta(\boldsymbol{\xi})/\partial\theta\): output-by-parameter Jacobian; \(\mathbf K_\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\): matrix-valued NTK for \(m\) outputs.

formulations.name: Pareto stationarity for multi-objective PINNs
formulations.meaning: Expresses first-order Pareto stationarity for competing differentiable PINN objectives.
formulations.purpose: Provides a multi-objective interpretation of residual, boundary, data, and other tasks.
formulations.relation: This is a first-order necessary stationarity condition under the usual differentiability/regularity assumptions; it does not by itself establish Pareto optimality.
